prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a low-speed head-on collision in Sugar Land, Texas, and has neck and back strain. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1072; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Please state your full name for the recording.
A: I'd rather not give my name on the recording, but you can use the claim file.
Q: That's fine. Can you confirm you were driving the vehicle involved in the collision in Sugar Land, Texas?
A: Yes, I was driving my sedan. I was heading down the two-lane road toward the shopping center.
Q: Can you describe what happened?
A: Another car crossed into my lane. It was a head-on collision, but it wasn't a hard hit. We were both going slow, maybe fifteen or twenty miles an hour, and we came together front to front.
Q: Did you lose consciousness or hit your head?
A: No. I didn't hit my head. I was shaken up, but I stayed awake and got out of the car on my own.
Q: Were you wearing your seatbelt?
A: Yes, the belt was on and it locked when we hit. I think that's why I didn't go through the windshield.
Q: Have you received medical treatment since the accident?
A: Yes. I went to an urgent care clinic that same afternoon. They said I had a neck and back strain and gave me muscle relaxers and some physical therapy referrals.
Q: Are you still experiencing symptoms?
A: Yes. My neck is stiff, especially when I turn to check my blind spot, and my lower back aches when I sit for long periods. Some mornings it's worse than others.
Q: Have you missed any work because of your injuries?
A: I missed two days and I've been working shorter shifts since then.
Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add to your statement?
A: Only that I want to be sure my repair costs and medical bills get properly documented. I've kept all the receipts.
Q: Thank you. This concludes the recorded statement.
A: Thank you.
